data.narrative:
Code Metal, a Series B-stage Defense & Security company, is evaluated against a comparison universe of 10 peers spanning public equities (2 comps: DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and private companies (8 comps, including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Defense Unicorns, Heven AeroTech, and TurbineOne). The target currently carries a $1.25B post-money valuation following $161M in cumulative capital raised.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $1.2B last post-money valuation and applying a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier for Series B advancement, implies a value of $2.4B. Peer-median analysis across five same-stage, same-sector comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The peer cohort exhibits substantial dispersion, reflecting heterogeneity in defense-tech positioning and maturity.

Triangulating these two methods produces a central valuation range of $1.7B (median), bounded by a low of $850M and a high of $2.7B. The current $1.25B valuation sits in the lower-middle portion of this range. Key uncertainties include the stage-progression multiplier's applicability given Defense & Security subsector variation, and peer comparability given differing technology focus and customer diversification. The $2.4B–$1.0B spread between methods reflects the method-level uncertainty inherent in private company valuation at this stage.
